profile.summary: DeepGene is a DNA foundation model that learns from a pan-genome graph rather than a single reference sequence, so that genetic variation across individuals is part of what it sees in pretraining. It is a transformer encoder with rotary position embeddings, built to handle sequences of different lengths. The pretrained model is fine-tuned for sequence classification tasks such as promoter prediction and the Genome Understanding Evaluation (GUE) tasks.
profile.summary_source_locator: Europe PMC abstract; README introduction and Model Fine-tuning; finetune.py

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: The model is a RoFormer, a transformer encoder with rotary position embeddings, pretrained as a masked language model. The code's default configuration has 12 layers, hidden size 768, 12 attention heads, a vocabulary of 4096 tokens and 5120 positions; pretraining builds the model from this default configuration. The pretraining data comes from a Minigraph pan-genome graph: the processing script reads the graph's sequence segments and edges and tokenises them with the repository's tokenizer.json, and pretraining uses subgraphs (default size 128). For downstream tasks the pretrained weights are loaded into a sequence classification model and fine-tuned, with MCC or F1 as the metric.
sections.source_locator: parse.py; configuration_roformer.py __init__ defaults; data_init.py load_dataset; finetune.py

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: One pretrained model is offered, as a Google Drive folder with no version or checksum. The fine-tuning code loads checkpoints named pretrain_params_epoch_N from a model directory, by default epoch 20. A result should record which Drive file and epoch it used and the repository commit; this page read commit 486343e5. The environment is old: Python 3.8, torch 1.7.1 with CUDA 11.0, and transformers 4.29.2.

facts.label: Model type
facts.value: Transformer encoder DNA foundation model pretrained by masked language modelling on pan-genome graph data, then fine-tuned for classification.

quotes.text: a model leveraging Pan-genome and Minigraph representations

facts.label: Architecture
facts.value: RoFormer (rotary position embeddings). Default configuration: 12 layers, hidden size 768, 12 attention heads, intermediate size 3072. GENEB describes it as a transformer encoder plus graph transformer.
facts.source_locator: README introduction; configuration_roformer.py; GENEB README model table

quotes.text: DeepGene employs the rotary position embedding

facts.label: Inputs
facts.value: DNA sequences tokenised with the repository's tokenizer.json (vocabulary 4096 by default). GENEB lists the tokeniser as BPE. Fine-tuning data are train.csv, dev.csv and test.csv files.
facts.source_locator: data_init.py; configuration_roformer.py; finetune.py; GENEB README model table

facts.label: Outputs
facts.value: Masked-token predictions in pretraining; class logits after fine-tuning, scored with MCC or macro F1.

facts.label: Parameters
facts.value: Not stated by the developers in the sources read (the scripts print the count at run time). GENEB, a third-party benchmark, lists 85M.

facts.label: Training data
facts.value: A Minigraph pan-genome graph. The README links a .rgfa file on Google Drive; the processing script reads a file named hprc-v1.0-minigraph-grch38.gfa.

facts.label: Known versions
facts.value: One pretrained model, distributed as a Google Drive folder without version labels.

strengths.text: Pretraining on a pan-genome graph is meant to capture variation across individuals and populations, which single-reference models do not see.

quotes.text: the capability to capture genetic variations across individuals or populations in the foundation models
we introduce DeepGene, a model leveraging Pan-genome and Minigraph representations

strengths.text: Rotary position embeddings are used so one model can handle short and long sequences. The authors report the best overall score on the 28 GUE tasks and good efficiency for its size; these are the developers' claims.

quotes.text: On the 28 tasks in Genome Understanding Evaluation, DeepGene reaches the top position in 9 tasks, second in 5, and achieves the overall best score.
DeepGene outperforms other cutting-edge models for its compact model size and superior efficiency in processing sequences of varying lengths.

strengths.text: Code is Apache-2.0, and the README links fine-tuning data for promoter prediction (prom_5000).
strengths.source_locator: LICENSE; README: Fine-tune with pre-trained model

limitations.text: Weights are only on Google Drive, without a version, checksum or licence.
There are no usage instructions beyond pointers to the scripts, and no inference or embedding example.
The scripts assume CUDA GPUs: fine-tuning sets cuda:0 at start-up and pretraining is hard-coded for four GPUs. The pinned stack (Python 3.8, torch 1.7.1+cu110) is old.

no_run_guide_reason: The README gives no commands: it points to the scripts ("Please see PanGeneGraphTrans/finetune.py") and to Google Drive downloads. The scripts expect a checkpoint directory layout (pretrain_params_epoch_N) and data paths that the README does not document, so a run guide would have to invent paths and flags.
notes: The README links a .rgfa file while data_init.py reads hprc-v1.0-minigraph-grch38.gfa. The paper was later published in IEEE/ACM TCBB (DOI 10.1109/tcbbio.2025.3614354, PMID 40996989, not open access per Europe PMC); only the preprint abstract was read. GENEB vendors a copy of this repository and lists DeepGene as 85M, human. Coverage is limited because there is no model card and only the abstract of the paper was read.
